source_refs.note: iii. Filtration: a main subheading of 33.6 Wastewater Treatment, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 256-256.

blocks.text: Once the bulk of the solids has been removed, the water undergoes filtration. This is a mechanical process designed to remove the remaining fine suspended matter and some microorganisms. In a standard treatment plant, water passes through layers of graded sand and gravel. The sand acts as a physical barrier, trapping particles within the pores between grains. For more advanced purification, activated carbon is used.
